questions.question_text: For the pre-trained base models you build on, how are they tracked and monitored, for example for published vulnerabilities? Who owns this?
questions.evidence_prompt: The inventory of pre-trained base models you build on with source, version and owner, the vulnerability or advisory monitoring method and its latest review record, and any action taken on a finding, if any.

questions.question_text: For your highest-criticality customer-facing AI applications, how is customer input, including appeals and requests for a human to override the AI, captured and acted on after go-live? Who reviews it?
questions.evidence_prompt: For each highest-criticality customer-facing AI application, the channel for customer feedback, appeals and human-override requests, a recent log extract of items received and their outcomes, and the named reviewer and review frequency.

questions.question_text: For your highest-criticality AI systems, how are answers re-tested after go-live for accuracy, bias and security, for example through red teaming? How often is this done?
questions.evidence_prompt: The post-go-live re-test plan for each highest-criticality AI system (accuracy, bias, security, red teaming), its frequency, the latest test report with findings and actions, and the date of the last run.

questions.question_text: For your highest-criticality AI systems, how does a deletion or correction request reach the data the AI retrieves and its index? Where is this recorded?
questions.evidence_prompt: The deletion and correction request procedure showing how it reaches retrieval data and its index for each highest-criticality AI system, and the latest request log entry showing completion, if any.

questions.question_text: For your highest-criticality AI systems, how is a change to what the AI can do, for example a new tool, a new permission, a changed configuration or the removal of something no longer needed, approved and made after go-live? Who approves it?
questions.evidence_prompt: The change approval records for the latest change to tools, permissions or configuration (including removals) of each highest-criticality AI system, the approver, the change procedure, and the post-change check.

questions.question_text: For your highest-criticality AI systems, how is the model's behaviour re-checked after an update to the hosting stack, for example servers, GPU drivers or serving software? Who approves the rollout?
questions.evidence_prompt: The change procedure for hosting stack updates (servers, GPU drivers, serving software), the post-update behaviour test results for the latest update to each highest-criticality AI system, and the rollout approval with approver and date.

questions.question_text: For your highest-criticality customer-facing AI applications, how is customer feedback turned into measurable improvements in each update? Who decides which feedback is acted on?
questions.evidence_prompt: For each highest-criticality customer-facing AI application, the log of customer feedback with decisions on what to act on and who decided, the improvement measures set, and the latest release note showing a measured result.

questions.question_text: For the models behind your most critical AI systems, how are changes to how the model is built or tuned, and new versions, reviewed and approved before release? Who approves them?
questions.evidence_prompt: The change and release approval records for models behind critical AI systems (build or tuning changes, new versions), the named approvers, and the latest approved release with its review evidence.

questions.question_text: Before you release a new version of your model to others, how are the people who receive it engaged, for example to collect their feedback or tell them what changed?
questions.evidence_prompt: The communication to recipients of the latest released model version (release notes, change summary, feedback channel), the log of feedback collected, and the procedure that sets how recipients are engaged before a release, if any.

questions.question_text: For your highest-criticality AI systems, when answers are found to be wrong, biased or inconsistent, how is each fix, for example a change to prompts, data, the model or rules, re-tested to show a measurable improvement? Who signs it off?
questions.evidence_prompt: For the latest wrong, biased or inconsistent answer found in each highest-criticality AI system, the fix record (prompt, data, model or rule change), the before/after re-test results showing improvement, and the sign-off with name and date.

questions.question_text: For your highest-criticality AI systems, how is a wrong, biased or manipulated AI result, or an unexpected action by the AI, recorded as an error or incident, for example a wrong decision made on AI output or a leaked prompt? Who reviews it to find the cause?
questions.evidence_prompt: The AI error and incident register or ticket category for the highest-criticality AI systems, the latest recorded entry with cause analysis and reviewer, and the reporting procedure that covers the areas in scope, such as agents, tools and code generation.

questions.question_text: For your highest-criticality AI systems, when the AI gives a wrong or harmful result or takes an unexpected action, how are the people affected told? Who decides what is communicated?
questions.evidence_prompt: The procedure and decision rule for telling people affected by wrong or harmful AI results or unexpected actions, the named decider, and the latest notification sent or drafted, if any, covering the AI systems in scope.

questions.question_text: How does a problem with a vendor's AI feature, for example a wrong result or an exposure of your data, get from the vendor to your organisation and into your incident records? Who on your side follows it up?
questions.evidence_prompt: The route by which vendor AI problems reach you (vendor contact, notification clause in the contract or DPA), the latest vendor-reported issue recorded in your incident log, and the named person who followed it up, if any.

questions.question_text: When an error or incident is found in a model you have released, how are the people who received it told? Who decides what is communicated?
questions.evidence_prompt: The notification procedure for recipients of a released model with error or incident, the named decider, the recipient contact list, and the latest notice sent, if any.

questions.question_text: For the models behind your most critical AI systems, how do you keep a record of changes to the model or its setup and the reason for each change? Where is it kept?
questions.evidence_prompt: The change log or model registry history for the most critical models showing each change to the model or setup, the reason, the approver and date, and where the log is kept and who can edit it.

questions.question_text: How are incidents and near-misses from AI use nobody approved, or from other people's agents reaching your systems, recorded and communicated to those affected? Who reviews them afterwards?
questions.evidence_prompt: The record of incidents and near-misses from unapproved AI use or outside agents reaching your systems, the latest entry showing who was told and the post-incident review, and the procedure for recording and communicating them, if any.

questions.question_text: For your highest-criticality AI systems, when sensitive data sent to the AI is found to have been exposed, how are the affected people, providers and regulators told? Who decides who must be told?
questions.evidence_prompt: The notification procedure for exposed sensitive data sent to an AI, the decision record on who must be told (affected people, providers, regulators) with the decider, and the latest notification or exercise record, if any.

questions.question_text: For the infrastructure that hosts your most critical AI models, how are incidents such as compromise, outage or cost abuse recorded, communicated to those affected and reviewed afterwards? Who leads the review?
questions.evidence_prompt: For infrastructure hosting the most critical AI models, the incident log entries for compromise, outage or cost abuse, the communication sent to those affected, and the latest post-incident review with its lead, if any.

description: AI RMF area questions: every question that could be asked per mapping row (AI area x subcategory, data/ai/mapping.json), keyed by subcategory. A question lists the rows it covers (one question may stand for several areas' rows), the roles it is asked of and any producer flags; build_ai_questions.py picks a client's questions by filtering on their AI areas, role and producer flags. rows_sha is the hash of the subcategory's mapping rows the questions were written for; rows gives each row's area and impact (for the covers note and the evidence prompt). Recorded by record_ai_bank.py questions.
